exercises.prompt: You walk the entire length of the Earth's equator (about 40,000 km) at a steady 5 km/h, 24 hours a day with no breaks (ignore oceans). Roughly how long does it take?
exercises.explanation: 40,000 km ÷ 5 km/h = 8,000 hours, and 8,000 ÷ 24 ≈ 333 days. Walking only 8 hours a day it would take about three years.

exercises.prompt: If you could drive straight up to the Moon (about 384,000 km away) at a constant 100 km/h without ever stopping, roughly how long would the trip take?
exercises.explanation: 384,000 ÷ 100 = 3,840 hours, which is 160 days — a little over five months.

exercises.prompt: An Olympic swimming pool is 50 m long, 25 m wide and at least 2 m deep. Roughly how many liters of water does it hold? (1 cubic meter = 1,000 liters.)
exercises.explanation: 50 × 25 × 2 = 2,500 cubic meters, and each cubic meter is 1,000 liters, so 2.5 million liters.

exercises.prompt: The digits 0-9 we use in the West are usually called 'Arabic numerals'. In which region did this positional system with a symbol for zero originally develop?
exercises.explanation: The system arose in India and was transmitted to Europe through Arabic-language mathematicians such as al-Khwarizmi — hence 'Hindu-Arabic' numerals. The name credits the messengers, not the inventors.

exercises.prompt: Which came first on Earth: sharks or trees?
choices: Sharks, by tens of millions of years
Trees, by tens of millions of years
They appeared at roughly the same time
Trees, but only by a few thousand years
exercises.answer: Sharks, by tens of millions of years
exercises.explanation: The first sharks appeared roughly 450 million years ago; the earliest true trees only about 385 million years ago.

exercises.prompt: Exactly one letter of the alphabet does not appear in the name of any of the 50 US states. Which letter is it?
exercises.explanation: Every other letter shows up somewhere, from J (New Jersey) and X (Texas, New Mexico) to Z (Arizona); Q is the only letter that never appears.

exercises.prompt: True or false: shaving makes hair grow back thicker and darker.
choices: False — it only looks that way because a cut hair has a blunt tip
True — the follicle responds to the cut
True, but only for dark hair
False — shaving makes hair grow back thinner
exercises.answer: False — it only looks that way because a cut hair has a blunt tip
exercises.explanation: Shaving doesn't touch the follicle beneath the skin. The stubble feels coarser because the blunt cut end hasn't been tapered by growth or wear.

exercises.prompt: True or false: you lose most of your body heat through your head.
choices: False — the head loses heat roughly in proportion to its small share of body surface
True — about 80% of heat escapes through the head
True — the brain generates most of the body's heat
False — the head loses no heat at all
exercises.answer: False — the head loses heat roughly in proportion to its small share of body surface
exercises.explanation: The head is about 7-10% of body surface area and loses heat in proportion. The myth stems from a flawed old military study in which subjects wore cold-weather gear on everything except their heads.

exercises.prompt: In a group of 5 people, what is the probability that at least two of them were born in the same calendar month? (Assume all 12 months are equally likely.)
exercises.explanation: The chance that all five months differ is (12·11·10·9·8)/12^5 ≈ 0.382, so at least one match has probability ≈ 0.618 — the birthday paradox in miniature.
